extracted.intended_audience: emerging and practicing documentary photographers, photojournalists, and photography students
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and practical standards for producing long-form documentary photography projects and working ethically in the field, drawn from a four-hour conversation with Sebastião Salgado. Covers technique, project framing, ethics, fieldwork habits, and archival practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-intellectualizing photography
rubrics_metrics.description: Resist turning photography into an over-intellectualized exercise or operating as if you must present a philosophical justification for every image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Salgado expresses disdain for over-intellectualization—focus on making strong work rather than excessive theorizing about being an 'artist.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Make pictures well (good light and composition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs must be well made — good light and good composition — in order to contribute meaningfully to public discussion and endure over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Salgado argues that the circulation and impact of work like Sahel depend on the pictures being compelling; technical and compositional quality is central to documentary effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photograph suffering with dignity and respect
rubrics_metrics.description: Images of human pain should be brutally frank yet respectful and seemly, conveying dignity even in the most reduced circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Galeano's commentary: even skeletons or near-corpses can be shown 'with dignity' so photography both reveals and redeems human experience rather than exploiting it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not be detached — live within the situation
rubrics_metrics.description: Detachment is a disaster for the documentary photographer; instead, immerse yourself in the situation and let it become part of your life so you can share it authentically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Salgado: stay engaged with subjects; ethical concerns should be decided ahead of time so involvement does not equal exploitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide ethical concerns in advance
rubrics_metrics.description: Set your ethical stance before entering a situation so there is 'no room for doubt' about how you will behave and what your intent is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This pre-determined ethical framework guides choices in the field (when to photograph, when not to, how to explain your presence) and prevents opportunistic exploitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask permission and obtain introductions
rubrics_metrics.description: You must always ask permission to be part of a situation; when arriving in a community get introductions to whoever can grant permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not every shutter click needs explicit permission, but you should be accepted into the story first; explain yourself in a way that makes your presence meaningful to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Get inside the story — live with the subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: To tell a true documentary story you must get inside the story: live with the people, become part of the community, and let the project be your real life for its duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This depth allows you to know when it's appropriate to photograph and when it is not, and produces stronger, more honest work than superficial visits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know the framing and heart of your project
rubrics_metrics.description: Before and during fieldwork, be clear about what you want to do and why — the framing and core reasons for the project are crucial to sustaining it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your motives aren't central to you, difficulties on the ground can derail commitment; know the main threads of the story and hold to them while remaining open to specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do thorough research and develop contacts ahead
rubrics_metrics.description: Do as much research as possible before going into the field and develop contacts for introductions in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preparation both identifies story threads and smooths the process of gaining access and trust once you arrive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be nimble in the field while staying focused
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep eyes and mind open to unexpected realities, but remain focused on your main story threads and be prepared to adjust plans as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Salgado warns that things rarely unfold as expected; adaptability prevents losing the story and ending up with only a few nice but disconnected pictures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise restraint — know when not to photograph
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect people and moments by sometimes choosing not to make a picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Salgado explicitly says there are times he does not make the picture out of respect for the people and the moment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progressive intimacy / lens-length bell curve
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach a story gradually: begin more distant (longer lens), make introductions and gain acceptance, then move in (shorter lens) as people drop defenses; at the story apex you will be closest and making your best pictures, then extricate yourself gracefully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Salgado draws a bell curve showing how lens length shortens as trust increases, then lengthens again as the story winds down; this is both a tactical and ethical pattern of engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commit to long-term, multi-year projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Multi-year projects (examples: seven years) enable depth, coherence, and the freedom to pursue personal vision beyond assignment constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-term commitment is costly and hard to fund but affords autonomy from editors and allows a project to mature into a sustained statement (Salgado's Migrations, Workers, Genesis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use light as a personal signature and master exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a personal approach to light and understand how to use it expressively (Salgado often shoots against the light and overexposes Tri-X up to five stops).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Salgado's upbringing informed his sense of light; technical experimentation (e.g., high overexposure) can create distinctive results and should be understood and controlled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value contact sheets and archival practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Preserve negatives/contact sheets and avoid destroying or discarding images on the spot; archives can yield discoveries decades later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ritchin and Salgado value film archives (Salgado's archive exceeded half a million images); digital 'destroy-on-the-spot' habits can undermine serendipitous rediscovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer evolution of images over instant deletion
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow images to evolve in editing/viewing contexts rather than judging and deleting immediately on location; sometimes strong images are overlooked initially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ritchin's preference for seeing evolution frame by frame supports keeping material for later re-evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use photography to communicate and help — not to take
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach work with the intent to 'make pictures' that communicate and potentially help people/situations rather than 'take' from subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Salgado emphasizes motive: you must not go to exploit; pictures are a tool for communication and assistance, and sometimes subjects ask to be photographed as a way to be heard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage in humanitarian support and advocacy where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Where possible, support causes connected to your subject matter (donate time/money, collaborate with organizations) and use work to advocate for preservation or aid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Salgado donates to MSF, rehabilitated rainforest in the Amazon, and engaged in polio-elimination projects; projects like Genesis were conceived to restore faith in humanity and argue for conservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve creative control through independent funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Where feasible, seek funding models that free you from assignment constraints so you can express your vision directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Salgado values the emancipation from assignment work that long-term personal projects afford, even though funding seven-year projects is difficult.
